Workflow-based navigation

Creating navigation that highlights core use-cases.

Roles
Lead product designer, UX engineer
Tools
Figma, Storybook, Angular, HTML, CSS
Team
1 product designer/UX engineer, 2 developers
Timeline
Design Nov 2023 - Apr 2024; development and implementation through Aug 2024

Overview

Sourcescrub customers were analysts seeking difficult-to-obtain private-company data. The product exposed complex searches and many possible workflows, making key paths difficult to discover and remember.

Goal

Understand which workflows mattered most and make them the primary entry points in the main navigation, improving the customer experience and reducing training demands.

User research

Usage data from Pendo and Datadog was combined with input from Customer Success and revenue teams to identify the workflows that were most important, least discoverable, or most expensive to train.

UI design and implementation

Competitor patterns were reviewed before choosing a rail-and-drawer approach inspired by Material 3. The design focused on large workflow categories, expandable drawers, and an intentional hover delay. Working Angular components and Storybook documentation gave developers a usable foundation.

Release and response

The new navigation launched in phases with hand-picked vanguard customers. Feedback was strongly positive, and no customers asked to return to the legacy UI after receiving access to the new experience.

“The new UI is the EASIEST version of any deal origination software I've used so far.”
